scope: Disposable native Worker -> private MessagePort -> production TypeScript bridge -> Tauri raw binary IPC -> Rust StorageSession -> real SQLite diagnostic on Linux. Fixed fixture space, automation profile only, never production content, user data or the editor. Not production authorization, lifecycle, editor integration or desktop parity.

supersedes.description: First passing variant: 15 checks with bytes as JSON number arrays. Its evidence file is preserved in git history.

transport.requests: storage_read and storage_write take an application/octet-stream body through tauri::ipc::Request. The only application header is x-affine-ticket; any other x-affine-* header, a JSON body or a duplicated ticket is rejected. Write frame: u32 little-endian identifier length, UTF-8 identifier, update bytes. storage_close and storage_reopen keep a deny_unknown_fields JSON ticket request.
transport.responses: storage_read returns tauri::ipc::Response with a 9-byte header (status byte, i64 little-endian millisecond clock) followed by the document bytes.
transport.fallbackDetection: The page records console.warn output and the smoke fails if Tauri reports that the custom-protocol IPC failed and it fell back to postMessage.

limitations: Disposable fixture: one fixed space, automation profile only, e2e and storage-probe both required, debug only. It is not the production command boundary.

The ticket is a bearer token delivered to the main document, not frame identity. Same-origin code inside the renderer realm can use the granted commands; frame-src none in this fixture CSP narrows that exposure but does not prove content isolation.
Worker raw IPC (constructed Tauri IPC requests from a Worker) is not tested; the Worker merely has no bootstrap globals.

The native write path copies the body once more (decode_write) and the read path builds one response Vec; the 16 MiB bound is enforced by the core after the whole body is received. Aggregate queue memory, browser structured-clone allocation and read-side budgets are not measured. Only one 8 MiB document was exercised, so large-document compatibility is not established.

Document replacement is tested only for an idle session on a real reload. The new document explicitly drains the old session through storage_reopen; native lifecycle hooks that close the session on navigation, failed navigation, crash, BFCache or window close are not implemented or tested.
The generation pin is fixture policy, not a production ownership model.
Close failure is not injected; accepted-but-pending work across document replacement is not tested.
Linux only here. The CI stage reports other platforms separately; no Windows result for this diagnostic exists yet.
No snapshot or subscription transport, blobs, indexing, sync, awareness or telemetry, and no editor connection.
